notes:
Background: Riverglen builds an in-app product analytics assistant and contextual help widget. Evaluating Redwood to replace existing LLM API provider (current: OpenAI) — goal is Hosted for quick parity POC, then Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation.

AE/SE thread: Maya intro (9/15) -> SE deep dive (9/22) -> Demo (10/22) -> Security sync (10/29). SE noted: Redwood has OpenAI-compatible endpoints but recommends migration checklist to avoid prompt regressions.

POC summary: live parity tests on 3 canonical prompts sets (support, summary, rerank). Hosted API baseline: lower median latency vs current provider (~20% improvement) for short prompts; long-tail prompts show 10-30% variance. Key finding: reranker score deltas — some prompt rewrites needed; tokenization/stop-sequence behavior differs slightly.

Quotes: "We like the cost/latency numbers but saw a small blind spot on our product-rerank tests — can't ship regressions to customers." — VP Eng.

Security & compliance: require SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention 3+ years, KMS integration for key management, data residency in us-east. Legal team asked for sample DPA & SLA; billing/legal review in parallel with POC.

Operational asks: compatibility layer for OpenAI calls (minimal code change), function-calling parity, structured output enforcement, and deterministic sampling knob for stable evaluation across rollouts. Redwood suggested using local prompt wrappers and an eval harness to catch regressions before traffic rollouts.

Next steps (short): 1) Run 2-week Hosted parity POC with expanded prompt corpus (deadline 11/15). 2) Capture token-level diffs and run A/B on small % traffic. 3) Provide Dedicated sizing estimate for 2 GPUs reserved (throughput target ~180 requests/sec, 95th latency <250ms). 4) Legal & security to sign off on DPA/SLA and KMS integration.

Notes on pricing: asked for committed discount tiers and burst capacity terms. Preliminary estimate given (range in Drive deck). AE to deliver final pricing by 11/07.

Stability Risks: prompt-parity regressions on subtle instruction changes, mismatch in probability mass for reranking leading to drop in NDCG on tail items. Engineering wants a rollback plan + auto-fallback to current provider for critical queries.

migration_notes: Current provider: OpenAI (prod). Context: want minimal code churn via OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Compatibility layer: Redwood hosted supports OpenAI-compatible routes but function-calling and structured outputs require small wrapper changes; team prefers wrapper over app-level prompt rewrites.

Prompt parity: tokenization/stop-sequence differences introduced 3%+ delta on reranking metrics in initial tests; suggested mitigations: canonicalize tokenization, add post-processing comparator, use deterministic sampling for eval.
Regressions: identified 14 prompt cases with reduced rerank NDCG; SE recommended targeted prompt rewrites and a guardrail in Redwood Console to flag regressions during rollout.
Fallover strategy: staged canary on Hosted with automatic rollback to current provider for flagged regression thresholds, then plan lift-and-shift to Dedicated once parity + legal sign-off complete.
cost_expectations: Looking for 20-30% cost savings vs current provider at 1M tokens/month with committed Dedicated capacity; open to hybrid of Hosted + Dedicated for burst handling.
decision_criteria: 1) parity on rerank/summary quality across full prompt set; 2) predictable latency at 95th <250ms; 3) contractual data residency + KMS; 4) committed pricing within ARR range; 5) smooth migration path (compat layer) and rollback plan.
notes_short: Mid-market SaaS; evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated migration. POC shows promising latency & cost but prompt-parity/regressions need addressing. Security/legal in parallel.
